si_4_title.answer: Mapping the neuroanatomical heterogeneity of OCD using a framework integrating normative model and non-negative matrix factorization

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study utilized Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) to establish a normative model based on healthy controls, which was then applied to patients to calculate individualized neuroanatomical deviations (Z-scores).
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: we trained a Gaussian process regression model to predict voxel-wise GMV from age and sex in HCs and then applied the trained model to infer GMV of patients with OCD.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Han2023.pdf.md: Methods / Modeling latent disease factors

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The normative model was applied to voxel-wise gray matter volume (GMV) derived from T1-weighted MRI using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analysis.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: subject-level morphological (gray matter volume, GMV) differences were derived using the normative model. ... Individualized GMV differences were derived from the normative model and then parsed into latent disease factors using NMF.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Han2023.pdf.md: Methods / Overall approach; Fig. 1 caption

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age and sex were used as the primary explanatory variables (predictors) to model the normative distribution of gray matter volume in healthy controls.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: we trained a Gaussian process regression model to predict voxel-wise GMV from age and sex in HCs
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.location: Han2023.pdf.md: Methods / Modeling latent disease factors
